Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.: 207/19 Fir no.: 283/18 Ps : Pul Prahlad Pur U/s : 279/338 Ipc Neetu v. Sachin Pratap Cnr No.: Dlse01-001879-2019 Ms. Neetu W/o Rishi R/o Gd-53, Pul Prahladpur, New Delhi. ......Claimant/Petitione Versus 1. Sachin Pratap S/o Om Prakash R/o Village & Post-Bharoli Faridabad, Haryana. ............Driver/Respondent no 2. Sajjan Kumar S/o Manphool Singh R/o Police Post-Sec.28, Faridabad, Haryana. .........Owner/Respondent no. texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. Brief facts of the case are that on 16.11.2018 petitioner alongwith her husband Rishi Kumar and son Sagar were going to Jeewan Hospital, Sunlight Colony, New Delhi. At about 10.30 am, when they were crossing the road, offending vehicle bearing no. HR-51T-5119 (Hero Honda Splender motorcycle) suddenly came at a very fast and negligent manner and hit her. Due to such accident, she sustained grievous injuries and fracture. Injured/ petitioner was removed to Jeewan Hospital where her MLC bearing no. 371/18 dated 16.11.2018 was prepared and she remained hospitalized at said hospital till 19.11.2018. Thereafter, she took treatment as OPD till four months from the said hospital. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 12.04.2022 noticing 03% permanent physical impairment in relation to left upper limb. 3. An FIR in question bearing No. 283/18 u/s 279,338 IPC PS Pul Prahladpur, New Delhi was registered in this case. 4. As per record, R-1 and R-2 appeared on some dates but thereafter stopped appearing. Even they did not file any reply and their right to file reply was closed vide order dated 02.12.2019. Further, there was no insurance of the vehicle in question as per record. 5. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 02.12.2019 by my Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal: MACT No. 207/19 Neetu v. Sachin Pratap Page No. 2 of 20 BK 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 16.11.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-51T-5119 being driven by R1 and owned by R2? OPP. 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 6. Petitioner filed her examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. She relied upon various documents Ex.PW1/1 to Ex.PW1/6. As per record, PW-1 is not cross examined by R-1 or R-2. Neither they led any evidence.
texts.arguments: At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. A person MACT No. 207/19 Neetu v. Sachin Pratap Page No. 3 of 20 BK is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. It may be noted that in this background that in Cholamandlam Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD-Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s the relevant section is sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 18. Before proceeding further, it may be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. Sachin Pratap Page No. 5 of 20 BK (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) Further, as also argued by Ld. Counsel for petitioner that in case of present nature in which there is permanent disability also some guess work can also be employed having regard to the attending facts and circumstances. 28. It was further observed by Hon'ble SC in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 29.
